extractedText: Samsung-Hynix 50x, KOSPI 150x: Crypto Exchanges Become Korea Stock Betting Arenas3x KOSPI ETF Combined with Futures Leverage Bybit and KuCoin Follow Binance in Listings Trading Volume Surges as Investor Safeguards Fall ShortMarkets|Published 2026.06.29. 06:30:05|By Do Hye-won|Summary|SaveAAAOfficials check the KOSPI and major stock price indexes at Hana Infinity Seoul, located at Hana Bank's headquarters in Jung-gu, Seoul, on the 26th. The KOSPI plunged more than 8% during intraday trading that day, triggering a circuit breaker. Reporter Oh Seung-hyunUltra-high-risk derivatives based on Korean stocks are appearing one after another on overseas cryptocurrency exchanges. As investment demand to ride the KOSPI's rally grows, high-multiple products that would be difficult to permit domestically are circulating virtually without limit through overseas crypto exchanges. Concerns are mounting that domestic investor funds are flowing out to overseas platforms, and that losses, when they occur, are difficult to protect within the domestic regulatory framework.According to the financial industry on Friday, Binance recently launched a perpetual futures product called "KORUUSDT" based on "KORU," a 3x leveraged KOSPI exchange-traded fund (ETF) listed on the U.S. stock market. The product is structured to use Tether (USDT) as margin to invest in KORU price movements. Binance expanded the maximum leverage, which was 20x in the early listing period, to 50x on the 26th.Considering that KORU itself is designed to track KOSPI movements at 3x, the addition of 50x leverage could generate gains or losses up to 150 times the KOSPI's rate of change. If the KOSPI rises slightly, large profits can be made, but conversely, even a small decline can lead to an investment being liquidated in an instant.Binance is also rapidly expanding its lineup of derivatives related to the Korean stock market. On the 2nd of this month, it listed perpetual futures products with Samsung Electronics, SK hynix, and Hyundai Motor as their respective underlying assets. All three products initially allowed trading with up to 20x leverage, and the maximum multiple for products related to Samsung Electronics and SK hynix has now risen to 50x.Other global exchanges have joined the same trend. Bybit and KuCoin listed KORUUSDT perpetual futures this month and offer trading with up to 20x leverage. Bybit is considered a large cryptocurrency exchange with a significant share of global derivatives trading, and KuCoin is also a global crypto exchange that has grown on the basis of overseas users.Trading volumes are also growing rapidly. According to data compiled by global charting platform TradingView, KORUUSDT recorded $754.4 million in trading, or about 1.1604 trillion won, from the 22nd, when trading began, through the 26th. The cumulative trading value of SKHYNIXUSDT reached $6.4213 billion since its launch through the 26th, approaching 10 trillion won. HYUNDAIUSDT and SAMSUNGUSDT also recorded trading values of $473.58 million and $52.83 million, respectively, over the same period. The industry believes that a significant portion of this may be demand from domestic investors.The barriers to access are low. Domestic investors can trade these products by buying Tether with won on won-market exchanges such as Upbit or Bithumb and then transferring it to an overseas exchange wallet. Unlike the stock market, there is no closing time, so trading takes place 24 hours a day.The problem is that the regulatory gap widens as domestic investment demand moves to overseas exchanges. Funds betting on the direction of the domestic stock market flow to overseas platforms, and trading fees also end up going to overseas operators. There are also concerns that taxation blind spots may arise given the nature of trading using overseas accounts.There is also a large gap in the level of investor protection compared with domestic products. For a retail investor in Korea to invest in leveraged ETFs or exchange-traded notes (ETN), they must undergo prior education and meet a basic deposit requirement of 10 million won. In contrast, perpetual futures on overseas crypto exchanges are difficult for domestic financial authorities to supervise directly, making it hard to apply the same level of safeguards.Major countries abroad already strictly manage access to global crypto exchanges. The United States and Japan restrict their own users from directly using Binance's global platform, requiring services to be provided through separate entities subject to local regulation. This is the backdrop for voices in Korea saying that the situation, in which overseas derivatives trading is in effect used as a bypass route, should not be left unchecked.Kim Min-seung, head of the Korbit Research Center, said, "Such products can have a psychological impact on domestic investors in that prices move even after the domestic market closes."
